me.title: Hi, Dino here!
me.p1: I am a web developer with five years of experience in the job market. During this time, my main focus has been frontend development; however, over the past two years, I have been dedicated to studying and building backend solutions, especially since I started college and became a student at
me.p2: My intention with this space is to share my experience through my journey and the projects I have been developing.
me.p3: If you would like to learn more about my work, please feel free to get in touch with me through my social networks. Best regards!

p1.partOne: I have always been someone who spent time imagining what my life would be like when I turned 30. For a long time, I saw myself teaching music and making a living from it. After all, playing music was what I loved the most, and for a while, it was also a source of income — especially during college, which was the period when I invested the most in pursuing a career as a musician.

p2.partOne: But it wasn’t always like that. From 2009 to 2012, I was focused on reading and trying to teach myself how to program, since I had always been interested in computers, technology, and understanding how things worked.
p2.partTwo: At that time, I found some programming materials about
p2.partThree: through torrents, but the concepts, principles, and programming logic never really clicked for me.
p2.partFour: Looking back, I believe I was too worried about money — or rather, the lack of it — and because of that, my mind wasn’t free enough to absorb something new.

p3.partOne: Thankfully, that changed in 2019, ten years after my first attempt. It was by watching classes from Professor
p3.partTwo: that I truly began to understand the world of programming.

p1.partOne: The first time I heard about programming was in 2011, after telling a friend that I wanted to improve my math skills. He suggested that I could learn math by studying programming. At that time, I was 22 years old.

p2.partOne: He gave me some materials on a flash drive, including handouts and video lessons. The first one I read was about
p2.partTwo: and another about VisualG and I didn’t understand anything at all. I tried to learn programming, but it simply didn’t click.

p3.partOne: Programming logic didn’t make sense to me. I desperately needed a job, had no idea what I wanted to do in life, and didn’t even know how to study. A lot of time passed after that attempt. During those years, I worked different jobs, dropped out of one degree, and started another — a Bachelor's in Music — all within an eight-year period.

p4.partOne: I didn’t mention this before, but I’ve always been interested in technology. I enjoy solving problems and working with logic — what I lacked was practice. I’ve always been curious about how computers and the internet work.

p5.partOne: In 2019, after graduating, I was teaching music theory and classical guitar in Teresina, Brazil. The main reason I decided to change careers was the extremely low salary — it didn’t even reach

p6.partOne: Later that year, around September, I was at home studying guitar when I suddenly remembered programming. I immediately stopped, grabbed my laptop, and opened YouTube.

p7.partOne: Fortunately, programming content had improved a lot between 2012 and 2019. There was a lot of high-quality free material available, and YouTube recommended the

p9.partOne: I deliberately went through these materials slowly — I didn’t want them to end. After finishing, I focused on programming fundamentals. Based on my wife's advice, who is also a developer, I chose a language to start building small projects.
p9.partTwo: I went back to the course and completed all

p10.partOne: At this point, the year had turned, COVID-19 had reached Brazil, and in 2020 I decided that programming would become my profession.

p11.partOne: In June, I saw an ad from
p11.partTwo: offering a full-stack web development course with scholarships up to 100%. There was only one full scholarship per state, so I gave it everything I had.

p12.partOne: A few days after taking the test, I found out I had been selected. I was incredibly happy — I still keep that document as a trophy.

p13.partOne: The course lasted 7 months, and I made the most of it. I started applying for jobs while still studying. I received many rejections, even with the market booming.

p14.partOne: For the final project, my team built a school management system. It was challenging — from database modeling to frontend integration — but we made it work. Presenting it was a huge achievement.

p15.partOne: After finishing the course, I felt a bit lost — which is normal after an intense learning period. I kept applying and getting rejected. I realized referrals worked better.

p17.partOne: On March 11, 2021, I received the news that I had passed the technical stage. I was extremely happy — but also scared. I thought: "I made it... now what?"

p18.partOne: The truth is, I overcame imposter syndrome and insecurity. Today, I have over five years of experience. I’ve gone through layoffs, changed companies, started a new degree, and joined curso.dev.

p19.partOne: My goal with this story is to motivate you. If you’re starting out or unsure about your abilities, remember:

p1.partOne: A very common practice in church life is that its members gather in small groups for the purpose of relating, sharing experiences, learning about God, among other things. As the church grows, it becomes necessary to manage these groups in some way, and the most common way is to use a spreadsheet.

p2.partOne: GC Manager is a web application designed to facilitate the management of
p2.partTwo: of the Angelim Teresina Church and its campuses. It allows the creation, editing, and deletion of groups, user management, and access control through permissions, among other features.

p3.partOne: One of the main features of this system is the ability to generate banners with the information of a GC. Previously, this work was done manualy using the online tool
p3.strongText: and all information was entered manually, taking around 8 minutes per banner.

p4.partOne: Later, when I took responsibility for updating GC information and generating banners, I created a script using JavaScript and
p4.strongTextOne: the time to generate a single banner dropped to less than 1 second!
p4.partTwo: This script fetched GC information from a
p4.partThree: file exported from Google Sheets and generated images using
p4.partFour: and the Node.js File System module.

p5.partOne: This only solved part of the problem. Now, other people need to handle this management, hence the need for a system that facilitates this work and is readily available on the internet.

mvc.title: MVC Architecture (Model-View-Controller)
mvc.description: Clear separation of responsibilities between business logic, user interface, and data flow control, facilitating maintenance, scalability, and testability.

docker.title: Docker Infrastructure
docker.description: Isolated and replicable environment using Docker and docker-compose, ensuring consistency across development, testing, and production environments.

database.title: Database Versioning
database.description: Database structure changes managed through migrations, allowing version history, safe rollbacks, and synchronization between environments.

quality.title: Code Quality and Standards
quality.description: Use of Prettier, linting rules, and Conventional Commits to maintain consistent code style, avoid common errors, and improve collaboration.

tests.title: Automated Tests
tests.description: Unit and integration tests executed automatically to ensure system reliability and safer deliveries.

auth.title: Authentication and Authorization
auth.description: Secure authentication with encrypted passwords, permission-based access control, and protected routes.
